probe_question: Can predecessor binding plus deterministic effect_id/payload_hash detection make two same-predecessor competing intents safe across intent-before-current and current-before-intent crashes without relying on a global compare-and-swap?

symbolic_model.current_pointer_rule_under_test: current is advisory only; restart authority comes from completed immutable successor self-certificates bound to e2
symbolic_model.revised_atomic_record: Each completed successor self-certificate embeds the same predecessor_epoch/effect_id/payload_hash triple that a separate intent would carry. A separate intent may be replicated for diagnostics but is not required to authorize restart.
restart_rule: Enumerate completed self-certified successors bound to e2; do not authorize from numeric generation or current pointer alone.
If no completed successor exists, remain at e2.
If every completed successor has the same effect_id and payload_hash, treat them as equivalent idempotent replicas and choose a deterministic representative.
If one effect_id appears with different payload_hash values, fail closed before replay/output.
If different effect_id values are bound to the same e2, classify as competing effects and fail closed before replay/output in this tested scope.

cases.intent_before_current: idempotent: completed successor certificates are equivalent even if current was never advanced
cases.current_before_separate_intent: idempotent only when the already-durable successor self-certificate itself embeds (e2,x,h1); the missing separate intent is non-authoritative

cases.intent_before_current: fail closed once both completed predecessor-bound certificates are visible; current cannot break the tie
cases.current_before_separate_intent: fail closed after restart if both completed certificates embed their payload hashes; a current pointer that lacks the embedded triple is insufficient

cases.intent_before_current: fail closed; deterministic lexical ordering would silently discard a semantically distinct effect and is not accepted
cases.current_before_separate_intent: fail closed only if both completed successors remain discoverable and self-describe their predecessor/effect/payload; last-writer-wins current is never sufficient

negative_control.protocol: two-record protocol where current can become authoritative before the predecessor/effect/payload triple is durable in either an immutable intent or the successor certificate
negative_control.reason: A crash can expose an apparently admitted successor while the conflicting intent is absent. Deterministic effect_id/payload_hash comparison has no evidence to compare, so predecessor binding alone cannot detect the hidden conflict.

result.static_restart_claim: For a finite already-durable candidate set, predecessor binding plus embedded effect_id/payload_hash certificates is sufficient to make duplicate proposals idempotent and conflicting proposals fail closed without a global CAS. Both interruption orders are restart-safe only when the successor certificate is durable before current and carries the full conflict-detection triple.
result.live_concurrency_limit: Not solved: after restart scans a currently finite candidate set and authorizes one result, a late writer may still publish another completed successor bound to e2. Without a fence/CAS/deadline that closes the predecessor to new proposals before any user-visible or irreversible effect, static conflict detection does not prove exactly-once live execution.
result.mechanism_revision: Collapse intent identity into the immutable successor self-certificate and demote current to an advisory cache. This removes the current-before-separate-intent crash gap, but it does not by itself close the late-writer race.

tested_scope: One symbolic certified predecessor e2; two completed successor proposals; three relation classes (same effect/same payload, same effect/different payload, different effects); two crash orderings (intent-before-current and current-before-separate-intent); current treated as advisory; immutable successor certificates assumed enumerable at restart.
untested_or_unresolved: A proposal that appears after restart selection/authorization (late-writer race)
Concurrent user-visible or irreversible side effects before predecessor closure
Incomplete directory enumeration or transient transport reads
Garbage collection of losing successor certificates
More than two writers or arbitrary replica counts
Malicious certificate forgery or compromised clock/scheduler identity

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local immutable certificate persistence and readback only; rate-limit interruption must checkpoint and resume across invocations rather than wait
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: Close the predecessor to late same-predecessor proposals before any externally visible effect without using a global CAS or richer execution service.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to frozen sanitized controls and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, protected-primary, hosted-compute, paid, finite-credit, or manual-user execution semantics were used.
exact_continuation: Next valid invocation: checkpoint first, then test exactly one cross-invocation predecessor-closure mechanism: predecessor e2 precommits a proposal deadline/slot and successor certificates are proposals only; a later scheduled invocation may authorize an effect only after the closed slot and only if every admissible predecessor-bound certificate is equivalent. Stress a late conflicting writer before vs after the precommitted deadline. Determine whether this bounded admission barrier removes the late-writer race without global CAS, waiting/polling, richer-mode execution, finite monthly quota, or user action. If clock/slot authority is insufficient, preserve that as the blocker and test a deterministic single-owner precommit alternative next time.
